operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: 'Store_ID', 'Store_Name', 'Type', 'Area_size', 'Number_of_product_category', 'Ranking', 'District_ID', 'District_name', 'Headquartered_City', 'City_Population', 'City_Area', 'Product_ID' — must be double-quoted verbatim; column lookup case-insensitive.
FK DDL uses backtick quoting (`Store_ID`) while CREATE TABLE uses double quotes; pragma foreign_key_list is authoritative, DDL text is not.
FK parent column case differs from child: child 'Product_ID' -> parent 'product'.'Product_ID' (parent DDL spells 'product_id'); pragma resolves it, so read_schema must not string-match.
All tables tiny (product 6, store 5, district 15, store_product 15, store_district 5) — no rowid sampling needed; original_values fully read.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes anywhere; only PKs. So drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op and NOT NULL insert failures never occur.
Composite PK on store_product (Store_ID, Product_ID); store_district has single-col PK Store_ID that is also an FK to store — PK/FK overlap.
store_district.Store_ID is PK and FK to store.Store_ID: parent values must be unique in the child, so FK draw with replacement then PK dedup will shrink rows.
product.dpi has distinct=1 (all 600.0) and interface distinct=1 ('USB 2.0') — Number/String samplers get a single element; list range collapses.
product.dimensions / max_page_size are text holding '301 x 160 x 158' / '216mm x 356mm' — String fuzzer will treat as generic text, not parse dimensions.
store_product.Store_ID distinct=4 (missing 4) and Product_ID distinct=5 (missing 5) — original FK coverage is partial; not a constraint.
All declared types are INT/REAL/TEXT — no Date/Time/Bool/Bit/Year dispatch, no crash-fallback columns, no text-stored dates.
No self-references, no dangling FKs, no views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all INT/REAL columns: scale=0 for INT (range [-1,1] then perturb +-1/+-2), scale=4 for REAL (range [-10^4,10^4]); list range overwritten to full max (upstream quirk) so REAL columns get huge values like 9999.x far from 179.84/94620.

String fuzzer on product, dimensions, max_page_size, interface, Store_Name, Type, District_name, Headquartered_City: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0..20 with 50% contaminate — destroys 'Fujitsu fi-6130...', 'City Mall', 'Attock District'.
String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) for int-like elements only; none of the text columns are int-like, so no numeric variants.
PK columns (product_id, Store_ID, District_ID) are single-col PKs -> max_l0=inf, so fresh Number draws never reused; PKs stay distinct, dedup rarely fires.
store_product composite PK members get max_l0=30; FK draws from parent's final PK values with replacement, then PK dedup keeps first occurrence — child rows collapse toward min(parent_size, n).
store_district.Store_ID PK+FK: FK draw with replacement from store.Store_ID (5 values) then PK dedup -> at most 5 rows regardless of chosen size.
choose_table_sizes: w.p. 0.5 flat int(30*u + u2*200) per table, else level sizes (level0 = 1+30u, x4 per level, cap 2500) — tiny DBs get 1..~2500 rows, wildly larger than originals (5-15).
No NOT NULL/CHECK/UNIQUE enforcement in Python; only PK dedup and (no-op) unique dedup — so no insert failures expected, rows_ok == chosen size (minus PK dedup).

Likely FN drivers: Number fuzzer's full-range overwrite makes REAL predicates (Area_size > 100, City_Population > 500000) trivially true/false; String fuzzer destroys LIKE '%District%' / 'City Mall' matches; dpi/interface single-value columns become random.

Likely FP drivers: tiny original tables (5-15 rows) mean many gold queries return 0 or 1 row; random instances with 1..2500 rows make COUNT/EXISTS/aggregate predicates differ; missing ties in originals (Ranking 1,2,3,9,10) vs random Ranking values change ORDER BY LIMIT results.
FK consistency preserved (parent final values), so join-cardinality queries (store JOIN store_product) keep referential integrity but with random multiplicities.
